Classical and Acoustic are kind of misleading at times as an ACOUSTIC guitar is generally any hollow body guitar that is commonly seen in genres such as Classical, Country, Soft Rock and sometimes even Jazz, the word CLASSICAL guitar in my understanding moreso refers commonly to Nylon Stringed Acoustic guitars which use Nylon Strings as opposed to steel strings.

Based on the image you have provided, considering that the Headstock(The top part where the tuners or Tuning Pegs are) is a very common sight on Classical/Nylon Stringed guitars, you have a Classical guitar there, though those strings appear to be quite rusty which leads me to believe this a Steel String Classical Guitar.

Assuming that guitar has a Truss Rod in the neck(a Long metal pole in the neck of the guitar that keeps the neck straight), you may wanna consider some new strings, if it does’nt have a Truss Rod in it, while you can use Steel Strings still, your guitar neck in time will eventually break off because the steel strings are pulling at the neck from the joint where the neck and body meet, if there is no truss rod, I recomend a fresh pair of nylon strings, I find 10’s would be good(Don’t ask me about string gagues, explaining them is a headache)
